accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief Election Commissioners of India:
1. V.S. Ramadevi was the first woman Chief Election Commissioner.
2. V.S. Ramadevi served in 1990.
3. V.S. Ramadevi was the tenth Chief Election Commissioner.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: V.S. Ramadevi was the first and only woman Chief Election Commissioner and served in 1990. T.N. Seshan, not Ramadevi, was the tenth CEC.
accepted.tq: Split the statements using the office-holder and numerical designation.
accepted.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

accepted.s: Which one of the following Chief Election Commissioners is particularly associated with election reforms, enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct and introduction of Elector Photo Identity Cards?
accepted.x: T.N. Seshan, the tenth CEC, is associated with major election reforms, enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct and Elector Photo Identity Cards.
accepted.tq: Match the notable reform with the correct office-holder.
accepted.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

accepted.s: The headquarters of the Election Commission of India is located at:
accepted.x: The Election Commission of India has its seat at Nirvachan Sadan, New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Test the exact institutional location rather than a nearby central-government building.
accepted.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the training arm of the Election Commission of India?
o: Law Commission of India, New Delhi
accepted.x: The India International Institute of Democracy and Election Management (IIIDEM), New Delhi, is the training arm of the Election Commission of India.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an institution's training arm from its headquarters.
accepted.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

accepted.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Election Commission of India
B. Golden Jubilee of the Election Commission
C. Diamond Jubilee of the Election Commission
D. Completion of 75 years of the Election Commission
accepted.x: The Election Commission was established in 1950, its Golden Jubilee was in 2001, Diamond Jubilee in 2010 and 75 years were completed in 2025.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the establishment year and then compare the anniversary years.
accepted.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

accepted.s: The Election Commission of India was established on:
accepted.x: The Election Commission of India was established on 25 January 1950.
accepted.tq: Separate the foundation date from neighbouring national and electoral dates.
accepted.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Golden Jubilee was observed in 2001. The Diamond Jubilee was in 2010 and 75 years were completed in 2025.
accepted.tq: Use anniversary arithmetic to eliminate swapped milestone years.
accepted.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

accepted.s:
With reference to post-retirement restrictions on Election Commissioners, consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution expressly bars retiring Election Commissioners from receiving any further government appointment.
2. The Constitution contains a bar on the post-retirement appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General.
3. Article 319 deals with post-retirement restrictions relating to the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Constitution does not expressly bar retiring Election Commissioners from further government appointment. Constitutional restrictions apply to the CAG under Article 148(4) and the UPSC Chairman under Article 319.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional-bar trap and distinguish ECs from CAG and UPSC provisions.
accepted.sec: Post-retirement restrictions - constitutional position

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the constitutional position regarding the qualifications and tenure of the Election Commissioners?
o: The Constitution prescribes a five-year term and qualifications equivalent to those of a Supreme Court judge.
The Constitution prescribes both detailed qualifications and a fixed six-year tenure.
The Constitution prescribes qualifications but leaves tenure entirely to the President.
The Constitution prescribes neither qualifications nor a term of office for them.
accepted.x: The Constitution prescribes neither qualifications nor a term of office for the Election Commissioners; these matters are dealt with through the applicable legal framework.
accepted.tq: Watch for the constitutional-versus-statutory distinction.
accepted.sec: Post-retirement restrictions - constitutional position

accepted.s: The CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 is identified as:
o: Act No. 49 of 2023, replacing the 1975 Act
Act No. 29 of 2023, replacing the 1991 Act
Act No. 49 of 2022, replacing the 1991 Act
Act No. 49 of 2023, replacing the 1991 Act
accepted.x: The 2023 law is Act No. 49 of 2023 and replaced the 1991 Act.
accepted.tq: Check both the Act number and the legislation it replaced.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s: Under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, the Search Committee is headed by:
accepted.x: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'who performs this institutional job?' method.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Search Committee under the 2023 Act:
1. It is headed by the Law Minister.
2. It includes two members of Secretary rank or above.
3. It prepares a shortlist of five names.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister, has two Secretary-rank or above members, and shortlists five names.
accepted.tq: Treat each composition and numerical detail as a separate statement.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s: Under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, which statement is correct regarding the Selection Committee?
o: It must select only from the five names shortlisted by the Search Committee.
It has no role in recommending names to the President.
It may select a person only after approval by the Chief Justice of India.
It may select names other than those included in the shortlist prepared by the Search Committee.
accepted.x: The Selection Committee may choose names outside the shortlist prepared by the Search Committee. It recommends the names for appointment by the President.
accepted.tq: Test the exception to the normal shortlist-based selection process.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s: The eligibility requirement under the 2023 Act includes which of the following?
o: A sitting Supreme Court judge with administrative experience
Only a serving Chief Secretary of a State with judicial experience
Present or past Secretary to the Government of India rank with election-management experience
Any member of Parliament with electoral experience
accepted.x: An eligible person must hold or have held a post equivalent to Secretary to the Government of India and possess election-management experience.
accepted.tq: Look for the exact rank-plus-experience combination.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s: The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act is:
o: Until the age of 70 years or five years, whichever is later
Five years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier
Six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
accepted.x: The tenure is six years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. Reappointment is not permitted.
accepted.tq: Compare both components of a compound tenure rule and note 'whichever is earlier'.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the service conditions of the CEC and ECs:
1. They are paid on a par with a Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. The CEC and the other Election Commissioners receive equal salaries.
3. Their service conditions may be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The CEC and ECs receive equal salaries on a par with a Supreme Court judge. Their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed-protection statement in a service-conditions question.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner?
o: The CEC may be removed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister alone.
The CEC may be removed by the Chief Justice of India on a judicial recommendation.
The CEC is removed by a simple majority of the Lok Sabha alone.
The CEC is removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge, through a special-majority address by both Houses of Parliament.
accepted.x: The CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge, on a special-majority address passed by both Houses of Parliament.
accepted.tq: Use the 'who would perform this constitutional removal?' test.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s: With regard to the removal of Election Commissioners other than the CEC, which one of the following is correct?
o: They can be removed only on the recommendation of the Chief Justice of India.
They can be removed by the Union Cabinet without any recommendation.
They can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC.
They enjoy an absolute constitutional immunity from removal.
accepted.x: Election Commissioners other than the CEC can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC. Section 11 of the 2023 Act provides the removal procedure.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the removal safeguards applicable to the CEC and other ECs.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s: Article 324(2) of the Constitution provides that the Election Commissioners are appointed by the President subject to:
o: A recommendation of the State Election Commission
A resolution of the Supreme Court
accepted.x: Article 324(2) vests appointment in the President, subject to the provisions of a law made by Parliament.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional article with its exact statutory qualification.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s: In Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2023), the interim selection panel directed by the Constitution Bench consisted of:
o: Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister, Law Minister and Chief Justice of India
President, Prime Minister and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
accepted.x: Until Parliament enacted a law, the Constitution Bench directed selection by a panel comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition or leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India.
accepted.tq: Separate the interim judicial mechanism from the later statutory mechanism.
accepted.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the principal change made by the 2023 Act in relation to the interim mechanism in Anoop Baranwal?
o: The entire Selection Committee was replaced by the Search Committee.
The Prime Minister was replaced by the President.
The Leader of Opposition was replaced by the Law Minister.
The Chief Justice of India was replaced by a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
accepted.x: The 2023 Act replaced the Chief Justice of India on the selection panel with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the CJI in the interim panel and the Cabinet Minister in the statutory panel.
accepted.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

accepted.s: Before the judgment in Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India, the appointment of the CEC and ECs was made by the President on the advice of:
o: The Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition and Chief Justice of India jointly
accepted.x: Before the interim mechanism laid down in Anoop Baranwal, the President appointed the CEC and ECs on the advice of the Prime Minister alone.
accepted.tq: Arrange the institutional position before, during and after the judicial intervention.
accepted.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

accepted.s: The Tarkunde Committee, which proposed a selection panel comprising the Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition and Chief Justice of India, was set up in:
accepted.x: The Tarkunde Committee was set up in 1975 by Jayaprakash Narayan and proposed a three-member selection panel and a three-member Election Commission.
accepted.tq: Link the committee's year with its distinctive proposed composition.
accepted.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

accepted.s: Who set up the Tarkunde Committee?
accepted.x: The Tarkunde Committee was set up by Jayaprakash Narayan in 1975.
accepted.tq: Test the person associated with the committee rather than its recommendation.
accepted.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tarkunde Committee:
1. It proposed a three-member Election Commission.
2. It proposed a selection panel of the Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition and Chief Justice of India.
3. It was constituted under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Tarkunde Committee proposed both a three-member Commission and the PM–LoP–CJI selection panel. It was set up in 1975, not under the 2023 Act.
accepted.tq: Reject the anachronistic statutory attribution in statement 3.
accepted.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

accepted.s: The constitutional challenge to the 2023 selection framework was pending, as of May 2026, in:
o: Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Jaya Thakur v. Union of India
accepted.x: The 2023 Act was challenged in Jaya Thakur v. Union of India, and the matter remained pending as of May 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the later statutory challenge from the earlier Anoop Baranwal judgment.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

accepted.s: Which concern was raised in the proceedings concerning the 2023 selection committee?
o: The use of a three-member Election Commission
The government having a 2–1 majority and the absence of one absolutely neutral person
The absence of any role for the President in appointment
The Search Committee having more members than the Selection Committee
accepted.x: The framework was criticised for giving the government a 2–1 majority. The Supreme Court also questioned the absence of one absolutely neutral person and asked whether the Leader of Opposition was merely ornamental.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional-balance concern rather than a formal appointment step.
accepted.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions
